questions.explain: Tool rules: one intent per tool (lookup_order, not run_sql), typed validated parameters, bounded results via @max_rows, idempotency keys on writes — and never give an agent raw SQL access.
options: Expose raw SQL so the agent is flexible
One intent per tool, validated parameters, bounded results, idempotency keys on writes; never raw SQL
One giant tool that does everything
Tools need no validation; the model is smart
questions.q: What are the design rules for agent tool functions?

questions.explain: Every mutating tool takes @idempotency_key; on replay the procedure returns the original result from dbo.agent_actions instead of double-applying — agents retry, so retries must be safe.
options: Idempotency keys are optional decoration
Disable retries entirely
Use transactions only
Every mutating tool takes @idempotency_key; replays return the original result instead of double-applying
questions.q: Why do mutating agent tools require idempotency keys?

questions.explain: The action log row is written in the same transaction as the action itself — if the action rolls back, the log entry rolls back too, so the log can never claim success for a failed action.
options: The action log row is written in the same transaction as the action itself
Log after commit in a separate transaction
Log only failures
The action log is optional
questions.q: What transactional discipline applies to the agent action log?

questions.explain: Auto-approve for low-stakes reversible writes; require approval (agent pauses as awaiting_approval) for money movement, external communications, and data deletion; denied for out-of-scope actions.
options: Approve everything automatically
Require approval for all actions
Auto-approve low-stakes writes, require human approval for money/comms/deletion, deny out-of-scope actions
Approvals are handled by the LLM
questions.q: What is the three-tier human approval policy for agent actions?

questions.explain: Each step is its own transaction with a compensating action recorded upfront; on failure the agent executes compensations in reverse order, using the agent_actions table as the saga log.
options: One big transaction for the whole workflow
Saga pattern: each step commits independently with a compensating action; failures trigger reverse-order compensation
No compensation needed; just retry
Manual cleanup by support staff
questions.q: How are multi-step agent workflows made safe with the saga pattern?
